hall-friendship-hours.name: Jeffrey Hall's study of hours it takes to make a friend
hall-friendship-hours.outcome: About 50 hours together to go from acquaintance to casual friend, 90 hours to friend, and more than 200 hours to close friend; based on 355 adults who had recently moved and 112 University of Kansas freshmen
hall-friendship-hours.limits: University press release about a study in the Journal of Social and Personal Relationships, not the paper itself; hours were mostly self-reported, and time spent working together counted for less than time hanging out.
hall-friendship-hours.locator: "more than 200 hours before you can consider someone your close friend"

epley-talking-to-strangers.name: Epley and Schroeder's commuter study on talking to strangers
epley-talking-to-strangers.outcome: In nine field and lab experiments, train and bus commuters who talked with a stranger reported a more positive commute than those who sat alone, though people predicted the opposite
epley-talking-to-strangers.limits: University press release about a paper in the Journal of Experimental Psychology: General; it measured single, brief conversations, not lasting friendships or loneliness over time.

harvard-adult-development.name: Harvard Study of Adult Development
harvard-adult-development.outcome: Followed 268 Harvard sophomores (later their children and other groups) for nearly 80 years; close relationships, more than money or fame, predicted lasting happiness
harvard-adult-development.limits: University news story about its own study; the original group was all men at one elite college, and the findings are associations, not proof that relationships cause health.
harvard-adult-development.locator: "Good relationships don't just protect our bodies; they protect our brains."

friendship-line.name: Institute on Aging Friendship Line
friendship-line.outcome: A 24/7 talkline for adults 60 and older and adults with disabilities (888.670.1360), with ongoing outreach calls to people who ask for regular check-ins
friendship-line.limits: Limited to people 60 and older, adults with disabilities, and their caregivers; regular outbound calls need an intake form. The organization's own page.
friendship-line.locator: "Ongoing outreach calls to individuals who request regular check-ins"

lifeline-988.name: 988 Suicide and Crisis Lifeline
lifeline-988.outcome: Call, text, or chat 988 any hour; the site lists emotional distress and needing someone to talk to as reasons to reach out
lifeline-988.limits: A crisis line, not a way to build lasting friendships; the launch year is not on the page.

mens-sheds-australia.name: Men's Sheds in Australia
mens-sheds-australia.outcome: The Australian Men's Shed Association, set up in 2007, supports more than 1,300 Men's and Community Sheds where men work on projects together
mens-sheds-australia.limits: The association's own homepage; the count is its claim, and this page reports no loneliness outcomes. The founding year comes from the association's history and a search summary, not this page.
mens-sheds-australia.locator: "supporting more than 1,300 Men's and Community Sheds"

parkrun-ireland-men.name: parkrun friendships among middle-aged men in Ireland
parkrun-ireland-men.outcome: Interviews with 39 men aged 45 to 64 who ran, walked, or volunteered at the free weekly 5k found friendships formed through repeated attendance and improved wellbeing
parkrun-ireland-men.limits: Small qualitative study in Health Promotion International (Dunne, Quirk, Bullas, and Haake); co-authors are linked to parkrun research, and it doesn't measure loneliness with a scale.
parkrun-ireland-men.locator: "Social connections were developed after repeated participation in parkrun"

happy-to-chat-benches.name: Avon and Somerset Police chat benches
happy-to-chat-benches.outcome: Police put benches in two parks with a sign inviting strangers to sit and say hello, aimed at older people at risk of isolation and scams
happy-to-chat-benches.limits: News report on the launch; no evaluation of whether it reduced loneliness, and it's unclear whether the benches are still in place.
happy-to-chat-benches.locator: "Sit here if you don't mind someone stopping to say hello!"

danmark-spiser-sammen.name: Denmark Eats Together (Danmark Spiser Sammen)
danmark-spiser-sammen.outcome: Twice a year, in weeks 17 and 45, clubs, libraries, homes, and local groups host shared meals, organized by the People's Movement Against Loneliness that Ældre Sagen helped start in 2014; Ældre Sagen says just over 600,000 Danes feel lonely
danmark-spiser-sammen.limits: The organizer's own volunteer page; it gives no attendance or outcome figures. The first campaign year may differ from the movement's 2014 start.
danmark-spiser-sammen.locator: "Hvert år i uge 17 og 45 deltager Ældre Sagen i"

big-lunch.name: The Big Lunch
big-lunch.outcome: Each June, neighbors across the UK share food on their streets and in gardens and community spaces; the organizer says millions have joined in
big-lunch.limits: The organizer's own page (Eden Project Communities); participation numbers are its own estimate, with no exact figure for a recent year, and no loneliness outcomes.

humanitas-deventer.name: Humanitas retirement home housing students rent-free
humanitas-deventer.outcome: Six university students lived rent-free among residents mostly over 80, in exchange for 30 hours a month as good neighbors
humanitas-deventer.limits: News report from 2015; small scale, and no recent source confirms the program still runs. Director Gea Sijpkes designed it.
humanitas-deventer.locator: "volunteer 30 hours a month in the home"

capitol-hill-cohousing.name: Capitol Hill Urban Cohousing
capitol-hill-cohousing.outcome: Nine apartments and 21 residents share a building and cook shared dinners on rotating teams, three or four nights a week
capitol-hill-cohousing.limits: One community described in a news story; cohousing usually takes years to plan and money to buy into, and this source reports no loneliness measure.
capitol-hill-cohousing.locator: "is home to nine apartments and 21 residents"

jumbo-kletskassa.name: Jumbo supermarket chat checkouts (Kletskassa)
jumbo-kletskassa.outcome: First chat checkout opened in 2019 in Vlijmen; its success led Jumbo to plan another 200, as part of a health ministry program against loneliness
jumbo-kletskassa.limits: News report on the announced rollout; the 200 was a plan, and no current count or outcome data was found.
jumbo-kletskassa.locator: "The first 'Kletskassa', or chat checkout, as it has been dubbed, was opened in 2019"

la-poste-facteur-visits.name: La Poste's mail carrier visits (Veiller sur mes parents)
la-poste-facteur-visits.outcome: The mail carrier visits an older person at home once a week on a chosen day and passes news to named relatives; from €23.90 a month, €11.95 after the tax credit
la-poste-facteur-visits.limits: A paid commercial service, described on La Poste's own page; the 2017 launch year comes from search results, not this page. No outcome data.
la-poste-facteur-visits.locator: "Chaque semaine, le facteur vous rend visite, chez vous"

timeleft-dinners.name: Timeleft dinners with strangers
timeleft-dinners.outcome: An app books you a group dinner or other outing with five new people, mixed by age range, personality, and language, in more than 200 cities
timeleft-dinners.limits: The company's own marketing page; it's paid and in cities only, and there's no independent evidence that tables become lasting friendships.
timeleft-dinners.locator: "The weekly gatherings turning strangers into friends."

bumble-for-friends.name: Bumble For Friends app
bumble-for-friends.place: Australia, Canada, Ireland, New Zealand, the Philippines, the UK, and the US
bumble-for-friends.outcome: A separate app, launched in 2023 from the BFF mode Bumble began in 2016, where people swipe through profiles with similar interests to find friends
bumble-for-friends.limits: Tech news story on the launch; free with paid upgrades, and no independent data on whether matches turn into friendships.
bumble-for-friends.locator: "originally launched BFF mode in the main app in 2016"

seoul-goodbye-loneliness-120.name: Seoul's Goodbye Loneliness 120 helpline
seoul-goodbye-loneliness-120.outcome: A city helpline open at any hour (dial 02-120, then 5) handled 3,088 calls in about six weeks from April 1, passing its goal of 3,000 for the whole year; 59% of callers were middle-aged
seoul-goodbye-loneliness-120.limits: News report on early call volume, not outcomes; it's part of a five-year city plan.

japan-loneliness-act.name: Japan's Act on loneliness and isolation
japan-loneliness-act.outcome: Act No. 45 of 2023 asks local governments to set up local councils on loneliness and isolation that bring together support groups and professionals
japan-loneliness-act.limits: Official English translation of the law; councils are something local governments should make an effort to set up, not a requirement, and the text reports no results. It took effect in April 2024 per secondary sources.

england-social-prescribing.name: Social prescribing in England's health service
england-social-prescribing.outcome: Since 2019, doctors can refer patients to link workers who connect them to gardening clubs, music groups, and other non-medical help; more than 3,300 link workers are employed
england-social-prescribing.limits: News explainer, not the NHS or the underlying Lancet Public Health study; a UCL page with the study figures blocked access, and sources give different referral counts. Access is uneven across groups.

surgeon-general-advisory.name: US Surgeon General advisory on loneliness and isolation
surgeon-general-advisory.outcome: About half of US adults report loneliness; lacking social connection carries a risk compared to smoking up to 15 cigarettes a day; it urges people to pick up calls from friends, eat together, and put phones away in conversation
surgeon-general-advisory.limits: News report on the advisory; the primary hhs.gov pages blocked access in this run. An advisory recommends, it doesn't fund anything.

friendship-bench-zimbabwe.name: Friendship Bench
friendship-bench-zimbabwe.outcome: Trained grandmothers and community health workers talk with people on park benches; 1,290,861 clients seen and 985 active peer support groups, per the program
friendship-bench-zimbabwe.limits: The program's own impact figures; it treats depression and common mental health problems, not loneliness as such, so it shows lay listeners and peer groups rather than a loneliness cure.
friendship-bench-zimbabwe.locator: "the grandmothers, community health workers and communities at the heart of our work"
